title: Existence of a Johnson–Lindenstrauss dimension threshold
statement:
Let $\varepsilon$ be a real number with $0 < \varepsilon < 1$, and let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. Then there is a threshold $k_0 \in \bbn$ such that for every target dimension $k \ge k_0$, every ambient dimension $d$, and every finite set $V \subseteq \bbr^d$ of at most $n$ points, there exists a linear map $f : \bbr^d \to \bbr^k$ that is an $\varepsilon$-JL embedding of $V$; that is, for all $u, v \in V$,
\[
  (1 - \varepsilon)\,\norm{u - v}^2 \;\le\; \norm{f(u) - f(v)}^2 \;\le\; (1 + \varepsilon)\,\norm{u - v}^2.
\]
hypotheses_covered: target dimension k at least the threshold k₀
finite point set V of cardinality at most n
replaced:
For any $0 < \varepsilon < 1$ and $n \ge 2$, there exists a threshold
$k_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $k \ge k_0$, every ambient
dimension $d$, and every set $V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ of at most $n$ points,
an $\varepsilon$-JL embedding $f : \mathbb{R}^d \to_L \mathbb{R}^k$ of $V$
exists.  In particular the target dimension is $O(\log n / \varepsilon^2)$.
